idea: Themed weeks, Economy day: a replacement written after the first script for this slot was held; written from the source, then corrected by an independent editor before voicing.
description: In rural Karnataka, a man working as a farm labourer earned ₹205 a day in 2014-15 against ₹286 for a construction worker: 72% as much. In 2024-25 it was ₹454 against ₹485: 94%. The 22-point gain was 2.6 times the all-India gain of 8.6 points.

The ratio rose in nine of the ten years and was level in 2020-21. Karnataka and Kerala (+21.2 points) gained most of the 19 states with both wages. Karnataka's farm wage went from 91% to 114% of India's average. Current rupees; the Short compares the two wages within each year. The table shows how much, not why.
source: Labour Bureau (Ministry of Labour and Employment), Indian Labour Journal, as published in the RBI Handbook of Statistics on Indian States 2024-25 (11 Dec 2025), Tables 112 and 113: average daily wage rates in rural areas, men, general agricultural labourers over construction workers, current rupees. India is the average of all quotations. State figures for 2020-21 cover ten months. Recent years can be revised. Blank on the map: Jammu and Kashmir (boundary changed 2019) and states with no figure for both wages.
